title: Count Substrings With K-Frequency Characters I
statement: Count the substrings of `s` (non-empty runs of consecutive characters) in which some letter shows up `k` or more times, and return that count. Substrings are told apart by their start and end positions, so the same text found at two places counts twice.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters only
notes:
## Intuition

Testing every substring with running counts is O(n²), about 4.5 million substrings for 3,000 letters. The condition only gets easier as a substring reaches further left: if `s[start..right]` holds some letter `k` times, so does every substring that starts earlier and ends at `right`. So for each `right` the good starts are `0 .. left - 1` for a `left` that never moves back. Keep the window `s[left..right]` not good, with every count below `k`. Then a new letter is the only one that can reach `k`, which says exactly when to shrink.

## Approach

1. `count` holds the letter counts of the window `s[left..right]`.
2. For each `right`, add `s[right]`, whose index from 0 to 25 is `letter`.
3. While `count[letter]` is at least `k`, the window is good and a later start may be too: remove `s[left]` and move `left` forward.
4. Now `s[left..right]` is not good, but every start before `left` gives a good substring ending at `right`, so add `left` to `total`.
5. Return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abacb"`, `k = 2`. At `right = 0` and `1` no count reaches 2, so `left` stays 0 and `total = 0`. At `right = 2` a second `a` arrives; removing `s[0] = 'a'` gives `left = 1`, so `total = 1` ("aba"). At `right = 3` the `c` brings no count to 2, and `total = 2` ("abac"). At `right = 4` a second `b` arrives; removing `s[1] = 'b'` gives `left = 2`, so `total = 4` ("abacb" and "bacb"). The answer is 4.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `right` and `left` each move forward at most n times.
- Space: O(1): 26 counters.

## Pitfalls

- Add `left` on every step, not only when the while loop moved it: earlier starts stay good as `right` grows.
- Only `count[letter]` needs checking, since every other count was below `k` before this letter arrived.
- Shrink with `while`, not `if`: the letter that reached `k` may sit several places after `left`, as in `"abb"` with `k = 2`, where both `a` and the first `b` must leave.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `count` | occurrences of each letter in `s[left..right]` |
| `left`, `right` | first and last index of the window |
| `letter` | index 0 to 25 of the letter `s[right]` |
| `total` | good substrings counted so far |

narration.2: count holds how often each of the 26 letters occurs in the window s[left..right].
narration.3: Every start before left will give a good substring for the current right.
narration.5: Extend the window one letter at a time on the right.
narration.6: Turn the new letter into an index from 0 to 25.
narration.8: Only this letter can have just reached k; while it has, the window is good and a later start may be too.
narration.9: Take the letter at left out of the window...
narration.10: ...and move the start one step right.
narration.12: Every start before left gives a good substring ending at right.
